personas.name: Dawn Okonkwo-Reilly
personas.who: 48, office manager at a 22-person engineering firm, volunteered for this in a Monday standup for the fourth year running. Confident with software, zero patience for it. She is the research's ORGANIZER exactly: 'a volunteer… mildly resentful at having been volunteered, and quietly anxious about a public failure.'
personas.context: Work laptop at 1280px, two hands, fluorescent office light, 15:40 on a Thursday with a call at 16:00. Teams is pinging. Chrome, six other tabs open, one of which she will accidentally close this one instead of.
personas.task: Draw for 22 people, keep the two married couples apart, and get 22 private links out into 22 separate DM threads before the 16:00 call.
personas.verdict: She got a correct draw in 34ms and the per-person message is the best thing in the app, genuinely paste-ready, no composing. Then she lost the entire thing twice: once by tapping Draw a second time (which silently reassigned all 22 people after she had already sent 9 links) and once by reloading the tab. She finished on the third attempt, 20 minutes late, and will not describe this as a good tool.
delights: Cold open to first draw with zero gates: no account, no email, no occasion picker. Time-to-first-draw is genuinely under a minute, which is the research's own benchmark.

'Copy their message' produces a complete 233 to 252 character message ('🎁 Ana, your Secret Santa draw for Family Christmas 2026 is ready! Open your private link…') rather than a bare URL. Measured across six people: 233/243/247/237/238/252 chars. Nothing left to compose.
The draw is correct and she could feel it, two-tap couple pairing produced 'Ana ⛔ Marcus' as a removable row, and the assignment honoured it.

frictions.what: Nothing is saved. Measured localStorage after a complete 6-person draw with exclusions: {} , 0 bytes. Reloading the page leaves names='' (0 chars), 0 exclusion chips, 0 link rows, results hidden. The roster, the couple rules and every unsent link are gone.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research names this itself: 'The draw survives a reload… Persisting the group and the draw locally is the single most conspicuous absence.' Dawn is sending 22 messages one at a time in another app; she will tab away, and on a work laptop a tab gets closed. Redrawing does not recover, it produces a different draw, so the nine links she already sent become wrong.

frictions.what: Tapping 'Draw names' a second time silently reassigns everyone. Measured: 6 of 6 assignments changed between draw #1 and draw #2, and the on-screen list is byte-identical because the rows are rendered in input order (Ana, Marcus, Priya, Dev, Chris, Grandma Jo) with no match shown. drawWarn stays hidden; the only feedback is the same 'Names drawn!' toast.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the app's own version of the category's most credibility-destroying failure, the research quotes 'Someone was picked twice and Justin didn't have a secret Santa.' Ours is worse in one way: it looks like nothing happened. An organizer who taps twice because the first tap did not seem to register has just invalidated every link already sent, with no warning and no undo.

frictions.what: Adding one latecomer destroys most of the exchange. Measured: draw for 6, add a 7th name, redraw, only 2 of 6 original links still resolve to the same person, and the app says nothing about which. The exclusion pair survived the edit only because both names were untouched.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research calls this 'the highest-value feature to add' and the moment 'an organizer decides whether the tool is any good.' Right now we fail it the same way the email competitors do, except silently.

frictions.what: There is no proof the draw is sound. After a successful draw the app shows 22 name rows and a hint that ends 'a determined you could peek. Don't. 🎅', no count, no 'everyone gives once, everyone receives once, nobody drew themselves, 2 no-match rules respected'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Verbatim from the research differentiators: 'Show the proof.' The correctness is already there and measured (500 fuzzed draws through the shipped helpers.js: 0 invalid, 0 self-draws, 0 exclusion violations), it is simply invisible, so it buys nothing against Elfster.

frictions.what: Sending is 22 separate manual copy-then-switch-app round trips with no record of who has been sent. The list gives no read/sent state, no 'copy all', no numbering.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the whole second half of her job and the app abandons her at exactly the point the research says it should carry her ('Delivery through the channel the group already uses'). With no persistence, losing her place means starting the whole exchange over.

frictions.what: Typing a single character into the names box after drawing hides the results. Measured: pressing one key sets #results.hidden = true; the 12 link rows remain in the DOM but are unreachable.
frictions.whyItMatters: Correcting a typo in someone's name, the most ordinary thing an organizer does, silently destroys the visible draw. She has to redraw, which changes everyone.

personas.name: Marcus Tiwari
personas.who: 31, a participant, not the organizer, and this is the only screen he will ever see of this product. Technically fluent but doing this with 20% attention. The research's PARTICIPANT: 'one-handed, standing in a hallway or sitting on a couch, very often with other people in the room, sometimes the very person they drew.'
personas.context: iPhone at 414px, one thumb, sofa, 21:30 on a December evening with one lamp on. Phone is in dark mode. Partner is on the other end of the same sofa.
personas.task: Find out who he got, and remember the budget.
personas.verdict: Best thirty seconds in the whole app. The link opened cold with nothing revealed, the 336×71px 'Tap to reveal your person' button was unmissable, and 'Priya' landed at 35.2px in pine green (#7ab589 on #1c1113, 7.72:1) against warm near-black. It felt like a small occasion. Then his partner leaned over and he had no way to cover it back up, and he closed the tab in a panic.
delights: Nothing is revealed on page load, verified across 14 link variants in both colour schemes, nameVisibleBeforeTap was false every single time. The research asks for exactly this and it is honoured without exception.
The event line 'Rowan Street Family Christmas 2026 · Budget: $25' is right there under his name, so the second question every participant asks is answered before he asks it.

It works with the network off. Verified: service worker 'santa-v14' active, went offline, cold-loaded the reveal link, it rendered, the Fraunces display font was already cached and loaded, and the reveal still worked.

frictions.what: Once revealed, the name cannot be re-covered. Measured after the tap: revealBtn gets .hidden, the listener is registered {once:true}, and the only remaining buttons on the page are the hidden organizer draw button and the QR dialog's Close. There is no hide, no re-cover, no auto-timeout.
frictions.whyItMatters: Straight from the research: 'Shoulder-safe by default… offer a hide control that returns the match to covered. People open these links in rooms containing the person they drew.' We built the careful half (no auto-reveal) and skipped the half that matters once someone walks over.

frictions.what: The drawn name is 35.2px (2.2rem, index.html:1274). The research specifies 'display size around 2.5 to 3rem so it is legible at arm's length in one glance', 40 to 48px.
frictions.whyItMatters: It is the one thing on the screen and it is 12 to 27% under the size the category research asked for. Cheap to fix and it is the money shot.

frictions.what: The reveal carries the event name and the budget but no date. Three weeks later 'when is this again?' is still unanswered.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research lists 'the exchange date/time on the reveal, so the link answers when is this again? three weeks later' as table stakes; every ranked competitor has it.

frictions.what: The link is a 235-character URL inside a 233 to 252 character message. In a group thread the preview truncates it, and there is no short form, no copy-the-code fallback and no QR he can hand to someone.
frictions.whyItMatters: The delivery channel is the whole architecture. A link that a messaging app can mangle is the one failure mode we have no server-side recovery for, see Priya below.

personas.name: Yusuf Haddad
personas.who: 67, retired, runs the family exchange for eleven people every year and is also a participant in it. Early cataracts and a mild essential tremor in the right hand, the research's 'grandparent with no smartphone' inverted: he has one, he just needs it to behave. This is the persona the comfort panel exists for.
personas.context: Android phone at 414px held in the left hand, right index finger doing the tapping and overshooting by 5 to 10px on a bad day. Kitchen, 07:20, low winter light, reading glasses on the other table.
personas.task: Set up the eleven-name family draw, then later open his own reveal link.
personas.verdict: The comfort panel rescued him as a participant and failed him as an organizer. On the reveal screen, Largest + Easier reading turned a 35.2px name into 52.8px and a 71px button into a 122×362px slab, with zero horizontal overflow and axe clean, a real, measurable win. On the organizer screen the same settings could not fix the one control he needed, because that control ignores the text scale almost entirely.
delights: The comfort button is in the header on the reveal page too, so he did not have to find the organizer screen to fix his text. Panel opened, seven groups, Done stayed on screen.

Largest + Easier reading on the reveal: name 35.2px → 52.8px, 'Marcus, you drew a name…' 17.6px → 26.4px, reveal button 71px → 122px tall and 362px wide, page overflow 0px, axe violations 0. He read it without glasses.
'Easier reading' swapped Fraunces for the system sans on the who-line, which he noticed and preferred.

frictions.what: The exclusion name chips, the one control that makes this app worth using instead of a hat, are 28px tall with an 8px gap and 13px text at default. At Largest text plus Roomy spacing they reach only 39px with a 10px gap. The studio's own floor is var(--tap) = 44px, and comfort settings cannot get them there because .chip (index.html:654) sizes itself from padding, not min-height.
frictions.whyItMatters: Twelve 28px targets 8px apart is a mis-tap machine for a tremor, and a mis-tap here does not fail loudly, it silently creates the wrong no-match pair (tap Ana, tap the wrong neighbour, done). DESIGN-SYSTEM.md rule 4 is 'Interactive targets are at least var(--tap) (44px)', and the panel's stated contract is 'Density moves space, never targets.' Turning the text all the way up leaves this control 5px short of the floor. The research's own prescription is 'Two-tap pairing', the two taps have to land.

frictions.what: Undoing a mis-tap is a 37×36px ✕ inside a list row, and every one of them is named 'Remove pair' (app.js:73) with nothing distinguishing which pair.
frictions.whyItMatters: The recovery target is smaller than the target that caused the error. There is no undo toast anywhere in this app, despite #toast.act and the .undo pattern being shipped in the base layer (index.html:793-811) and used by other apps in the portfolio.

frictions.what: The names box is a bare textarea whose only instruction is a placeholder ('One per line: Mom / Dad / Jessie / Stephen'). The moment he types his first character the instruction disappears, and there is no visible label above it, the card heading 'WHO'S IN?' is rendered at 12px uppercase.
frictions.whyItMatters: Measured: textarea#names has 0 associated <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby. The design system's own note says --t-micro is for 'uppercase section labels… never a sentence', so the only naming this field has is a 12px all-caps fragment that his eyes skip.

frictions.what: The comfort trigger itself is a 36×36px circle, and the tip pill next to it is 82×36.
frictions.whyItMatters: Deliberate studio chrome and consistent across 23 apps, but it is the first thing a tremor user has to hit before anything gets easier.

personas.name: Priya Ravindranathan
personas.who: 26, a participant in an office exchange, not technical, uses her phone for everything. Got her link forwarded twice, organizer → group chat → her, and by the time it reached her the URL had been clipped.
personas.context: iPhone 320px-class viewport in a bus queue, one hand, cold, gloves half off, 08:05, three minutes before she boards.
personas.task: Open her link and find out who she got.
personas.verdict: Complete dead end, and the app did not even tell her something was wrong. She landed on a screen headed 'WHO'S IN?' with a big empty names box and a red '🎁 Draw names' button, assumed she was supposed to do the organizing, and messaged the organizer to ask what she was meant to type.
delights: When the link is intact it is instant, no login, no verification email, no app install. That is the whole pitch and it lands.

frictions.what: Every malformed reveal link silently falls through to the organizer tool. Tested four ways, '#r.' alone, '#r.abc', a valid payload truncated by 12 characters, and '#Marcus', and all four rendered the organizer view with 'Who's in?' as the first heading and no error state of any kind (app.js:138-141: if decode returns null, init() just carries on).
frictions.whyItMatters: The research documents the competitor equivalent as a shipped recovery feature: SecretSantaOrganizer maintains a whole 'forgot link' page because people lose their link. Our architecture has no server to recover from, which makes the error message the entire recovery flow, and there isn't one. A participant handed the organizer's own tool cannot tell she has hit an error, and could plausibly type names and press Draw.

frictions.what: A decodable-but-empty payload produces a ceremonial reveal of nothing: ', you drew a name…' then '🎄  🎄'. helpers.js:68 only checks typeof obj.s === 'string', so the empty string passes validation.
frictions.whyItMatters: The one case where the app does detect a link is the case where it should have rejected it.

frictions.what: A name containing a long unbroken token pushes the reveal page sideways. Measured at 320px: santa = 'ana.smith@marketingdepartment.com' (33 chars) → 33px of horizontal document scroll. At 414px the threshold is 26 unbroken capital characters (32px of scroll), rising to 255px at 40 characters. .revealwrap .who (index.html:1267) and .event (1268) have no overflow-wrap, while .revealName (1274) does.
frictions.whyItMatters: Organizers paste from distribution lists, and an address or a long compound name is what comes out. The page body scrolling sideways is the one layout rule the studio treats as absolute.

personas.name: Nkechi Adeyemi
personas.who: 34, blind, VoiceOver on iOS and NVDA on a work ThinkPad, organizes a nine-person book-club exchange. Highly competent with well-built web apps and extremely quick to abandon badly built ones.
personas.context: ThinkPad with NVDA at 1280px, headphones, evening, keyboard only, no mouse at any point.
personas.task: Enter nine names, mark one couple as a no-match pair, draw, and copy nine messages.
personas.verdict: She could not confirm that the couple rule had been created, so she did not trust the draw and stopped. Every individual element is technically present and axe reports zero violations, the failure is entirely in state, naming and focus, which is exactly the class of defect axe cannot see.
delights: The tab order matches the visual order with no traps: prefs → tip → event → budget → names → the name chips → Draw → footer. All 8 base controls reachable, 0 unreachable.
axe (wcag2a/aa, 21a/aa, 22aa) returns 0 violations on the organizer screen after a full draw, and 0 on the reveal screen both covered and uncovered at Largest text.
'Names drawn! Send each link privately.' is announced, #toast is role=status aria-live=polite and it is the one thing the app says out loud.

frictions.what: The names field has no accessible name. NVDA announces 'edit, multi line, blank'. Measured: textarea#names has 0 labels, aria-label null, aria-labelledby null, the standard battery flags it as the app's single hard failure ({unnamed:['textarea#names'], placeholderOnly:['textarea#names']}).
frictions.whyItMatters: It is the first and most important field in the app. DESIGN-SYSTEM.md's non-negotiables open with 'every control has an accessible name.'

frictions.what: Selecting a name for a no-match pair announces nothing and throws focus away. Measured: pressing Enter on the 'Ana' chip leaves document.activeElement === BODY, because renderExclusions() calls picker.replaceChildren() (app.js:50) and destroys the focused button. The chip carries no aria-pressed (null) and the selected state is conveyed only by .chip.sel's accent fill (index.html:1262). Nothing is written to the live region.
frictions.whyItMatters: Two failures stacked on the app's second-most-important interaction: WCAG 2.4.3 (focus dumped to the document root on every tap, so she must tab back through the whole page to pick the second name) and WCAG 1.4.1/4.1.2 (state carried by colour alone, never announced). She literally cannot tell whether tapping 'Ana' did anything.

frictions.what: The failure message is silent. #drawWarn (index.html:1317) has role=null and aria-live=null; it is only shown by removing .hidden. With three people and one no-match pair the draw is impossible, verified, 40ms, warning text 'Those no-match rules make a draw impossible, remove one pair and try again.', and nothing at all is announced. No toast fires on the failure path (app.js:90-96 returns before the toast at 115).
frictions.whyItMatters: She presses Draw, hears nothing, presses it again. The app's async status must go through a live region, that is a stated non-negotiable, and the toast right next to it already is one.

frictions.what: The nine 'Copy their message' buttons and nine 'QR' buttons are identically named. Only the adjacent .grow span carries the person's name, and nothing associates them.
frictions.whyItMatters: Her list of buttons is 'Copy their message' nine times. Sending the right link to the right person is the whole remaining task, and the accessible names make it a counting exercise.

frictions.what: After a successful draw, focus stays on the Draw button and twelve new rows appear below it with no announcement beyond the generic toast, and no heading focus move.
frictions.whyItMatters: She knows something happened but not what or how much; 'Names drawn!' does not say nine links are ready.

personas.name: Tobias Lindqvist
personas.who: 39, runs the exchange for a twelve-person pub quiz team, phone permanently in dark mode, deliberately does the draw in the room so nobody has to be trusted with a group chat. He is the user the QR path was built for.
personas.context: Phone at 414px in forced dark, pub table at 20:45, warm low light, passing the phone round with people leaning in.
personas.task: Draw for twelve, then hold the phone up so each person scans their own QR in turn.
personas.verdict: The QR codes work and scan, but the dialog they arrive in looks broken in dark mode and gives him no way to tell whose code is on screen, with twelve identical 'QR' buttons he lost his place at person five and had to start the pass-around again.
delights: The QR actually resolves. Measured for a 235-character link: 61 modules at 4px per module, a 244px code inside the 300px canvas, 26,656 dark pixels, comfortably scannable. The canvas paints its own white ground, so the code is valid in dark mode even though the dialog around it is not.

The QR never overflows: even at the longest payload the field limits allow (40+40 char names, 60 char event, 30 char budget → ~315 char URL), the code stays at 73 modules × 3px. The encoder only throws past ~2,400 characters, which this app cannot generate.
Escape closes the dialog and it opens with focus already on Close.

frictions.what: The QR dialog heading is invisible in dark mode. index.html:1344 hardcodes color:#111 on the <h3>, and #qrDlg (1343) sets no background token, so the UA default paints it rgb(18,18,18). Measured contrast: 1.01:1. 'Scan for your private reveal' simply is not there.
frictions.whyItMatters: A modal with an empty band above a black-and-white square reads as a rendering bug, in front of eleven other people. It is also a hex literal in the app layer, which DESIGN-SYSTEM.md rule 1 forbids outright ('Tokens only, no hex'), and the research's whole aesthetic thesis is that dark mode 'is not optional' for this app.

frictions.what: The dialog never says whose code it is. The heading is the same static string for all twelve, the canvas has no aria-label, no role and no text content, and #qrDlg has neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby.
frictions.whyItMatters: Passing a phone round is the app's best offline story and it is unusable past about five people because there is no state on screen. It is also the only reason a sighted-but-distracted organizer would hand the wrong person the wrong match, the exact failure the whole product exists to prevent.

frictions.what: Nothing marks who has already scanned or been sent. No read state, no dimming, no ordering.
frictions.whyItMatters: Same root as Dawn's problem, felt harder here because the list is being worked through live in front of the group.

frictions.what: Silent caps. Pasting 200 names produced exactly 60 chips and 60 link rows with no message anywhere (helpers.js:12, `if (out.length >= 60) break;`), and names over 40 characters are cut mid-word, 'Bartholomew Fitzwilliam-Cholmondeley-Featherstonehaugh' became 'Bartholomew Fitzwilliam-Cholmondeley-Fea' (helpers.js:8). Case-insensitive dedupe also silently merges two real people: 'Chris', 'chris', 'CHRIS', 'Chris ' collapsed to one chip.
frictions.whyItMatters: Not his twelve, but a 70-person office draw would produce a complete-looking list of 60 links with 10 people erased, and any office with two Chrises loses one of them. The seating-chart review found the same class of defect and the research calls a discovered cap 'the emotional peak of the category.'

worksWell: The draw itself is correct and fast, and that is the app's strongest asset. 500 fuzzed draws through the shipped helpers.js: 0 invalid assignments, 0 self-draws, 0 exclusion violations. Verified end-to-end through the real UI by decoding all six generated links: everyone receives exactly once, nobody drew themselves, the Ana/Marcus rule honoured. 12 people in 34ms; 60 people with 29 no-match pairs in 40ms.

The reveal is the best-built screen in the app. Nothing shows on load in any of 14 tested link variants across both colour schemes; the tap target is 336×71px; the name lands at 35.2px in pine at 6.88:1 (light) and 7.72:1 (dark). It reads as an occasion rather than a form response.

The privacy architecture is real, not marketing. Each link's payload contains exactly two names, that person and their match, and nothing else; there is no roster, no email, no account and no network call. Verified by decoding every link from a six-person draw.

It genuinely works offline. Service worker 'santa-v14' installs and claims, and with the network cut a cold reveal link renders fully, including the cached Fraunces display font, and reveals correctly.
The copy-to-message pattern is exactly what the research prescribed: 233 to 252 character paste-ready messages, not bare URLs.

The comfort panel does real work where it can reach. On the reveal at Largest + Easier reading: name 35.2 → 52.8px, button 71 → 122px, 0px overflow, 0 axe violations. Encoding is robust across scripts, CJK, Arabic RTL, Greek, ZWJ-family emoji, curly apostrophes and a null byte all round-trip intact.
No horizontal overflow anywhere on the organizer screen: 0px at 320, 414, 1280, at Largest text and at Roomy spacing, and 0px again with 60 people and 60 link rows.
hurts: Nothing persists. 0 bytes of localStorage after a full draw; a reload empties the names field, the pairs and every unsent link. This is the defect every persona hit and the one the research already flagged as 'the single most conspicuous absence.'

A second tap on Draw silently reassigns all 22 people while the on-screen list stays byte-identical, because rows are keyed on input order and never show a match. Measured 6/6 changed with no indication.
The exclusion chips are 28px (39px at maximum comfort settings) against the studio's own 44px floor, 8px apart, and they are the app's differentiating control.
A broken or truncated reveal link drops the participant into the organizer tool with no error state at all, four malformed hashes, four silent falls-through.
The QR dialog heading is #111 on #121212 in dark mode: 1.01:1, invisible, and a hardcoded hex in the app layer.

The failure path is silent and hard to read: #drawWarn has no role and no aria-live, and .warn is overridden at index.html:1264 to 13.6px in --accent, measured at 3.66:1 against the warn background, under both the 16px body-text floor and the 4.5:1 contrast requirement, on the one message the organizer most needs.
The names textarea has no accessible name of any kind, the standard battery's only hard failure.
Every chip tap destroys and rebuilds the picker, dumping keyboard focus to <body> with no aria-pressed and no announcement.
Silent data loss at the edges: 200 names in → 60 out with no message; names cut at 40 characters mid-word; two people named Chris merged into one.
Printing produces a sheet that leaks the roster but not a single assignment, the link URLs are nowhere in the printed text, but the names textarea and the Draw button print.
mostWantedNext: Persist the group, the pairs and the draw in localStorage, and let the organizer reopen tomorrow, finish sending, and reuse the roster next year, the research names this as a feature two competitors charge money for.

Make redrawing an explicit, guarded act, and after any redraw show which people's links are unchanged and which need re-sending. This is the research's #5 differentiator and it is the same fix as the latecomer case.

A verification line under the results: 'N people · everyone gives once · everyone receives once · nobody drew themselves · N no-match rules respected', the correctness already exists and is invisible.
A 'hide again' control on the reveal, and lift the name to 2.5 to 3rem.
A real error state for a broken reveal link: 'This link is incomplete, ask whoever sent it to send it again.'
Sent-state on each link row, so a 22-person send can survive an interruption.
Paper Mode, printable fold-over slips, which the research calls out as the one thing no digital competitor offers, and which the current print path is a long way from.

scenarios.name: Standard battery
scenarios.method: node design/stress.mjs secret-santa, layout at 320/414/1280 plus largest-text and roomy, touch targets, hostile text and injection, numeric edges, 30 rapid primary clicks, 200 bulk adds, reload persistence, corrupt storage, keyboard reachability, axe after interaction, print, console errors.
scenarios.result: 1 hard failure. Layout 0px overflow at every width and comfort setting. Hostile text: 0 injected scripts, 0 injected imgs, title not hijacked, no poison rendered. 30 clicks in 633ms with no console errors. axe clean. Keyboard: 8 focusable, 0 unreachable, but textarea#names is unnamed and placeholder-only, the hard failure. Note the battery's persistence heuristic reports '374→314 chars (persisted)' here, which is a false pass: 314 is the empty baseline, and the app in fact stores nothing.
scenarios.defect: textarea#names has no accessible name. The reload check needs reading against the measured 0-byte storage, not on its own.

scenarios.name: Draw correctness, fuzzed through the shipped logic
scenarios.method: In-page dynamic import of ./helpers.js, 500 draws at n = 3..20 with floor(n/3) couple pairs each, every result checked with the app's own validAssignment() plus independent self-draw and exclusion scans.
scenarios.result: 0 invalid assignments, 0 self-draws, 0 exclusion violations, 28 correctly-detected impossible configurations out of 500. Separately verified end-to-end through the real UI: a six-person draw with one couple, all six links harvested by stubbing navigator.clipboard and clicking every Copy button, then base64-decoded, everyone receives exactly once, nobody drew themselves, the Ana/Marcus rule honoured.

scenarios.name: Per-link privacy, does one link leak the roster?
scenarios.method: Stubbed navigator.clipboard.writeText, clicked all six 'Copy their message' buttons, decoded each URL fragment and searched each message for every other participant's name.
scenarios.result: Each payload contains exactly {s, g, e, b}, the recipient and their match only. No roster, no assignment map, no third name. (A naive substring scan flagged 'Chris' in four messages; that is the word 'Christmas' in the event name, not a leak.) Message lengths 233/243/247/237/238/252 chars; URL 235 chars; base64 fragment 188 chars.

scenarios.name: Redraw after links have been sent
scenarios.method: Drew for six, harvested all six assignments via the clipboard stub, tapped 'Draw names' again, harvested again, and diffed.
scenarios.result: 6 of 6 assignments changed. The rendered list is byte-identical because rows are in input order and never display a match. drawWarn stayed hidden; the only feedback was the same 'Names drawn!' toast. Adding a 7th name and redrawing left only 2 of the 6 original links still valid, with no on-screen indication of which (regex for 'still valid|unchanged|re-send|changed' over body text: false).
scenarios.defect: A second Draw silently invalidates every link already sent, and the UI gives the organizer no way to notice.

scenarios.name: Persistence and interruption
scenarios.method: Completed a six-person draw with an exclusion pair, dumped localStorage, reloaded, re-read the DOM. Also typed a single character into the names box after a successful draw.
scenarios.result: localStorage after a full draw: {} , 0 bytes. After reload: names field 0 chars, 0 exclusion chips, 0 link rows, #results hidden. One keystroke in the names box sets #results.hidden = true (app.js:146), the 12 rows survive in the DOM but become unreachable, and any redraw reassigns everyone.
scenarios.defect: Total loss of the roster, the no-match rules and every unsent link on reload or on any edit after drawing.

scenarios.name: Malformed and hostile reveal links
scenarios.method: Cold-loaded 14 URL-fragment variants across light and dark: valid payloads, CJK/Greek/Arabic RTL names, 40-char names, an empty-string payload, an HTML/script-injection payload, '#r.' alone, '#r.abc', a valid payload truncated by 12 chars, and a bare '#Marcus'.
scenarios.result: Injection is safe, 0 injected imgs, 0 injected scripts, payloads render as literal text via textContent. All four malformed hashes silently rendered the ORGANIZER view with 'Who's in?' as the first heading and no error message of any kind. The empty-string payload passed validation (helpers.js:68 only checks typeof) and produced a ceremonial reveal of ', you drew a name…' then '🎄  🎄'. Separately: setting the hash on an already-loaded page does nothing at all, there is no hashchange handler, so init() never re-runs.
scenarios.defect: A truncated or mistyped link hands the participant the organizer's tool with no explanation; an empty payload produces an empty ceremony.

scenarios.name: Dark-mode QR dialog
scenarios.method: Drew for five, opened the QR for the longest name in both colour schemes, read computed styles off the dialog and its heading, sampled the canvas pixel data, and measured the WCAG contrast ratio.
scenarios.result: Dark: dialog background rgb(18,18,18), heading colour rgb(17,17,17), 1.01:1. The heading 'Scan for your private reveal' is invisible. Light: 21:1, fine. The code itself is valid in both (canvas paints its own white ground; 26,656 / 26,720 dark pixels). Close button 82×44. Escape closes. Canvas has no aria-label, no role, no text; #qrDlg has no aria-label or aria-labelledby.
scenarios.defect: index.html:1344 hardcodes color:#111 on a dialog that has no background token, a hex literal in the app layer that fails in dark mode at 1.01:1.

scenarios.name: Touch targets with real data, at every comfort setting
scenarios.method: Typed 12 names, measured every chip and button, then repeated at Largest text and at Largest + Roomy.
scenarios.result: Exclusion chips 28px tall, 13px text, 8px gap at default. At Largest + Roomy: 39px, 19.5px text, 10px gap. 'Remove pair' ✕ 37×36. 'Copy their message' 153×36 and 'QR' 45×36, .btn.small hardcodes min-height:36px (index.html:598) so these never grow with --ui-scale either. The studio floor is var(--tap) = 44px. 14 sub-44px targets on a 12-person draw at default; 8 still sub-44px at maximum comfort settings.
scenarios.defect: The primary pairing control cannot reach 44px even with the comfort panel turned all the way up.

scenarios.name: Keyboard and screen-reader path through the whole organizer job
scenarios.method: Tabbed the full order from #names, pressed Enter on a chip and read document.activeElement, inspected aria state on chips and on #drawWarn, drove a draw from the keyboard, and enumerated live regions.
scenarios.result: Tab order matches visual order, 0 traps, 8 focusable, 0 unreachable. Enter on the 'Ana' chip → document.activeElement === BODY (picker.replaceChildren at app.js:50 destroys the focused node), aria-pressed null, toast empty, no announcement of any kind. #drawWarn: role null, aria-live null. The only live region in the app is #toast (role=status, aria-live=polite), and the impossible-draw path returns at app.js:96 before ever reaching it. After a successful draw focus stays on #drawBtn.
scenarios.defect: Selecting a name loses focus to the document root and announces nothing; the failure message is never announced at all.

scenarios.name: Contrast audit of the app-layer overrides
scenarios.method: Computed WCAG ratios for every colour the app layer sets, against the surfaces they actually render on, in both schemes.
scenarios.result: .warn / #drawWarn: --accent #c75771 on --warn-soft #ffeddb = 3.66:1 at 13.6px (index.html:1264 overrides the base .warn at 679), fails 4.5:1 and fails the 16px body floor. Dark: #f990a5 on #3f2504 = 6.47:1, passes. .revealName pine: 6.88:1 light, 7.72:1 dark, passes. .revealNote --ink-2: 5.66:1, passes. QR h3: 1.01:1 dark, fails catastrophically.
scenarios.defect: Two app-layer overrides break contrast; one of them is on the app's only error message.

scenarios.name: Caps, dedupe and truncation
scenarios.method: Pasted 200 names; pasted 'Chris / chris / CHRIS / Chris  / Sarah / Sarah / <54-char name> / Dev'; drew each time.
scenarios.result: 200 names → exactly 60 chips and 60 link rows, drawn in 347ms, with no cap message anywhere on the page (helpers.js:12). The eight-line duplicate test → 4 chips: 'Chris', 'Sarah', 'Bartholomew Fitzwilliam-Cholmondeley-Fea', 'Dev', case-insensitive dedupe merged four lines into one person and the 54-character name was cut mid-word at 40 (helpers.js:8). No message in either case.
scenarios.defect: A 70-person office produces a complete-looking set of 60 links with 10 people erased; two colleagues who share a first name become one participant.

scenarios.name: Reveal-page horizontal overflow with real-world names
scenarios.method: Cold-loaded reveal links with names of increasing unbroken length at 414px and 320px, measuring documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth.
scenarios.result: At 414px: 20 unbroken capitals 0px, 26 → 32px, 30 → 95px, 34 → 159px, 40 → 255px. At 320px, 'ana.smith@marketingdepartment.com' (33 chars) → 33px. Lowercase narrow glyphs at 40 chars stay at 0px. .revealName (index.html:1274) has overflow-wrap:anywhere; .revealwrap .who (1267) and .event (1268) do not. The organizer link rows are safe, ul.plain .grow carries overflow-wrap:anywhere (index.html:702).
scenarios.defect: Two of the three reveal text lines lack the wrap rule the third one has; an email-style or all-caps name scrolls the page sideways.

scenarios.name: QR encoder at the payload sizes this app can actually generate
scenarios.method: Called qrcode(0,'M') in-page at payload lengths 100 → 3,000 characters and recorded module count, the app's floor(300/(count+8)) cell size, and the failure point.
scenarios.result: 100 ch → 49 modules @5px (245px code); 200 → 61 @4 (244px); 300 → 73 @3 (219px); 500 → 89 @3; 900 → 117 @2; 1,500 → 149 @1 (a 149px code with 1px modules, unscannable); throws 'code length overflow' at 2,400. The maximum payload the field limits permit (two 40-char names + 60-char event + 30-char budget) is ~315 characters → 73 modules @3px. The app cannot reach the degraded range.

scenarios.name: Impossible and boundary draws
scenarios.method: Three people with one no-match pair (mathematically unsolvable); two people; 60 people with 29 no-match pairs.
scenarios.result: Impossible case: correctly detected in 40ms after 3,000 shuffle attempts (helpers.js:31), message 'Those no-match rules make a draw impossible, remove one pair and try again.', it does not name the offending pair (checked: the warning text contains neither 'Ana' nor 'Marcus'). Two people: 'You need at least three people for a proper Secret Santa.' 60 people / 29 pairs: solved in 40ms, 60 valid rows. No console errors on any path.
scenarios.defect: Detection and performance are correct, but the message is generic where the research explicitly asks us to name the specific pair causing it.

scenarios.name: Print
scenarios.method: emulateMedia('print') on a completed six-person draw and on an uncovered reveal, then read computed display and the printed text.
scenarios.result: Organizer sheet: #results prints with 6 rows, but each row reads 'Ana Copy their message QR', the URLs are nowhere in the printed text (/#r\./ over body innerText: false). The names textarea prints (the full roster), and the '🎁 Draw names' button prints as a bordered box. Header, tip pill, toast and the comfort panel are correctly suppressed by the base print rules. Reveal sheet: the name prints as text in pine, legible without background graphics.
scenarios.defect: Ctrl+P on the organizer screen yields a page that exposes the roster and no assignments, worse than useless. There is no print affordance and no Paper Mode.

scenarios.name: Offline, cold, via the service worker
scenarios.method: Loaded the app, waited for the worker to activate, cut the network at the browser-context level, then cold-loaded a reveal link and revealed.
scenarios.result: Worker registered and active, cache 'santa-v14' present. Offline cold load rendered the reveal correctly ('Marcus, you drew a name…'), the Fraunces display font was already cached and reported status 'loaded', and tapping revealed '🎄 Priya 🎄'. 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests.

scenarios.name: Comfort panel driven end to end on the reveal screen
scenarios.method: Opened #swsPrefs from the header on a reveal page, clicked the Largest and Easier-reading labels the way a finger would, closed the panel, then revealed.
scenarios.result: Panel opens with all 7 groups; the footer (Reset / Done) stays inside the dialog; 0px overflow while open. After Largest + Easier reading: data-text=xxl, data-reading=easy, name 35.2 → 52.8px, who-line 17.6 → 26.4px, reveal button 71 → 122px tall × 362 wide, page overflow 0px, axe 0 violations. On the organizer screen the same settings take the exclusion chips only from 28px to 39px.
scenarios.defect: Nothing broken, but the panel cannot lift the one control that most needs it above the studio's own 44px floor.

fixes.title: Persist the roster, the no-match pairs and the draw in localStorage
fixes.rationale: Measured 0 bytes of storage after a complete draw; a reload leaves an empty names field, 0 chips and 0 link rows. Dawn lost a 22-person exchange twice this way, and redrawing does not recover because it reassigns everyone. The research already calls this out by name: 'The draw survives a reload… Persisting the group and the draw locally is the single most conspicuous absence,' and Giftster and the paid iOS apps monetize the reuse-last-year's-group feature this unlocks. Store {event, budget, names, exclusions, assignment} under one key, restore on init(), and use the base layer's [data-saved-flag] to say so quietly.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:132-155 (init, nothing is read at boot), app.js:78-116 (draw, nothing is written), app.js:142-148 (the input handler)

fixes.title: Stop a second Draw from silently reassigning everyone, and show what changed when it does
fixes.rationale: Measured: tapping Draw twice changed 6 of 6 assignments while the rendered list stayed byte-identical, because rows are keyed on input order and never show a match. Adding one latecomer left only 2 of 6 original links valid, again silently. Dawn had already sent nine links. The research names both halves, 'someone was picked twice and Justin didn't have a secret Santa' is the incumbents' credibility failure, and 'Add a latecomer without blowing up the exchange… show which links are unchanged and which two or three people need a new one' is our #5 differentiator. Once a draw exists, the button becomes 'Re-draw' with a confirm, and after any re-draw each row gets 'unchanged' or 'new link, re-send'.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:78-116 (draw always overwrites), app.js:149 (drawBtn listener), index.html:1316 (#drawBtn label)

fixes.title: Give a broken reveal link a real error state instead of dropping the participant into the organizer tool
fixes.rationale: All four malformed hashes tested ('#r.', '#r.abc', a payload truncated by 12 chars, '#Marcus') rendered the organizer view with 'Who's in?' as the first heading and no message. Priya messaged the organizer to ask what she was supposed to type. Our links are 235 characters and get forwarded through chat clients that clip them, and we have no server-side recovery, so the error message IS the recovery flow. The research documents the competitor equivalent as a whole shipped feature (SecretSantaOrganizer's 'forgot link' page). When isRevealHash() is true but decodeReveal() returns null, show 'This link is incomplete, ask whoever sent it to send it again' instead of falling through. Also reject empty s/g at helpers.js:68, which currently passes and produces '🎄  🎄'.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:138-141 (the silent fall-through), helpers.js:63-74 (decodeReveal accepts empty strings at line 68)

fixes.title: Bring the exclusion name chips to the 44px floor and give them a keyboard/SR state
fixes.rationale: Four defects on one control, and it is the control that makes this app better than a hat. Measured 28px tall × 13px text × 8px gap at default and only 39px at Largest + Roomy, against DESIGN-SYSTEM.md rule 4 (var(--tap) = 44px), so the comfort panel cannot fix it and Yusuf's tremor creates the wrong pair silently. Pressing Enter on a chip leaves document.activeElement === BODY because renderExclusions() calls picker.replaceChildren(), aria-pressed is null, and nothing is announced, so Nkechi cannot tell whether her first tap registered. Add min-height:var(--tap) to the picker chips, set aria-pressed, restore focus to the same name after the rebuild, and write 'Ana selected, now tap who Ana must not draw' to the live region.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:49-65 (renderExclusions + chip creation), app.js:50 (picker.replaceChildren destroys focus), index.html:1262 (.chip.sel, colour-only state), index.html:654 (base .chip has no min-height)

fixes.title: Announce and re-style the draw failure message
fixes.rationale: #drawWarn carries the only two things that can go wrong and neither reaches a screen reader: role null, aria-live null, and the impossible-draw path returns at app.js:96 before the toast at 115, so Nkechi pressed Draw into total silence. Visually it is 13.6px in --accent at 3.66:1 on --warn-soft, under the 16px body floor and under 4.5:1, on the one message the organizer most needs, and it is red in an app whose brand colour is red (the research warns 'destructive actions in Secret Santa should use a neutral outline treatment… or the user will misread the primary button'). Delete the app-layer .warn override so the base warn box applies, add role="alert", and name the offending pair the way the research asks: 'Ana and Marcus can't both be excluded here, with 3 people there is no valid draw.'
fixes.where: index.html:1264 (.warn override), index.html:1317 (#drawWarn markup), apps/secret-santa/app.js:84-96 (both failure paths)

fixes.title: Fix the QR dialog in dark mode and say whose code it is
fixes.rationale: index.html:1344 hardcodes color:#111 on an <h3> inside a dialog that sets no background token, so in dark mode it renders rgb(17,17,17) on rgb(18,18,18), measured 1.01:1, completely invisible. It is also a hex literal in the app layer, banned by DESIGN-SYSTEM.md rule 1. Tobias's pass-the-phone flow then compounds it: the heading is the same static string for all twelve people, the canvas has no aria-label/role/text and the dialog has no accessible name, so he lost his place at person five. Use tokens (background:var(--surface); colour from --ink), title the dialog with the person's name, 'Marcus, scan for your private reveal', set aria-labelledby, and give the canvas an aria-label.
fixes.where: index.html:1343-1347 (#qrDlg, h3 with color:#111, bare canvas), apps/secret-santa/app.js:158-173 (showQr takes only the url, never the name)

fixes.title: Give the names textarea an accessible name
fixes.rationale: The standard battery's single hard failure: textarea#names has 0 associated labels, aria-label null, aria-labelledby null, and only a placeholder, which NVDA reads as 'edit, multi line, blank' and which disappears for Yusuf the moment he types. Its only visible naming is the card heading 'WHO'S IN?', rendered at 12px uppercase with 0.9px tracking, which the design system itself says --t-micro must never be ('uppercase section labels… never a sentence', and the second card's h2 is a 51-character sentence at that size). Wrap it in label.f with a real 'Who's in? One name per line' span, or point aria-labelledby at the heading.
fixes.where: index.html:1300-1305 (h2 + unlabelled textarea), index.html:1309 (the 51-character sentence rendered as a micro-label)

fixes.title: Report the 60-person cap, the 40-character truncation and the duplicate merge instead of doing them silently
fixes.rationale: Measured: 200 pasted names produced exactly 60 chips and 60 complete-looking link rows with no message (helpers.js:12); a 54-character name was cut mid-word to 'Bartholomew Fitzwilliam-Cholmondeley-Fea' (helpers.js:8); and 'Chris / chris / CHRIS / Chris ' collapsed into one participant. A 70-person office draw therefore ships 60 links and erases 10 people invisibly, and any office with two Chrises loses one. The research calls a discovered cap 'the emotional peak of the category'; the seating-chart review found the identical defect class. Either lift the cap (60 people draw in 40ms, there is headroom) or say 'Added 60 to 140 more lines were not included', and flag merged duplicates as 'Two people called Chris? Add a surname.'
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/helpers.js:8 (slice(0,40)), helpers.js:9 (case-insensitive dedupe), helpers.js:12 (the 60 cap), reported nowhere in apps/secret-santa/app.js:79

fixes.title: Show the proof under the results, and add sent-state to each row
fixes.rationale: The correctness is already there and already measured, 500 fuzzed draws with 0 invalid assignments, 0 self-draws, 0 exclusion violations, and it is completely invisible to the organizer, so it buys nothing against the incumbents whose worst reviews are 'someone was picked twice.' The research asks for it verbatim ('Show the proof'). Same card, same fix for Dawn's other problem: 22 copy-and-switch round trips with no record of who has been sent, and no persistence to survive an interruption. Add a verification line ('22 people · everyone gives once · everyone receives once · nobody drew themselves · 2 no-match rules respected') and mark each row 'sent' when its Copy or QR button is used.

fixes.title: Add a 'hide again' control to the reveal and lift the name to 2.5rem
fixes.rationale: Marcus's partner leaned over and there was nothing he could do: the reveal listener is registered {once:true} at app.js:124-129 and the button is hidden, leaving no control on the page. The research is explicit, 'Shoulder-safe by default: never auto-reveal on page load, and offer a hide control that returns the match to covered.' We built the first half perfectly (verified: nothing shown before tap across 14 variants in both schemes) and skipped the half that matters in a room. Same edit: index.html:1274 sets 2.2rem (measured 35.2px) where the research specifies 2.5 to 3rem for legibility at arm's length. Drop {once:true}, keep the button in place as 'Hide', and raise the size.

fixes.title: Make Ctrl+P produce something useful, or suppress it, right now it prints the roster and none of the assignments
fixes.rationale: Measured with emulateMedia('print') on a six-person draw: the results list prints as 'Ana Copy their message QR' six times, /#r\./ appears nowhere in the printed text, and the names textarea prints the full roster alongside a bordered '🎁 Draw names' box. So the one sheet of paper this app currently produces exposes who is in the exchange and hides who has whom, the exact inversion of its purpose. DESIGN-SYSTEM.md's non-negotiables say print is tested by actually printing. Minimum: .noprint the draw controls and the roster and print the links as visible URLs. Better, and the research's headline differentiator: Paper Mode, fold-over slips, name outside, match inside the fold.
fixes.where: index.html:1190-1246 (base print block, the app adds no print rules of its own), index.html:1301-1305 (#names prints), apps/secret-santa/app.js:107-113 (rows render buttons, never the URL)

fixes.title: Grow the row buttons with --ui-scale and distinguish their accessible names
fixes.rationale: 'Copy their message' (153×36), 'QR' (45×36) and 'Remove pair' (37×36) all sit under the 44px floor and stay at 36px even at Largest text, because .btn.small hardcodes min-height:36px (index.html:598) rather than deriving from --tap. Nkechi's button list is 'Copy their message' nine times with nothing to tell them apart, and every 'Remove pair' ✕ carries the identical aria-label (app.js:73), so the recovery target for Yusuf's mis-tap is both smaller than the mis-tap and unnamed. Give each an aria-label carrying the person or pair ('Copy Ana's message', 'QR code for Ana', 'Remove Ana ⛔ Marcus'), and let the row controls use var(--tap) on touch.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:73-74 (Remove pair), app.js:109-112 (Copy / QR buttons), index.html:598 (.btn.small min-height:36px)

fixes.title: Wrap long tokens on the reveal, and handle a hash set after load
fixes.rationale: Two small correctness gaps on the participant screen. .revealName (index.html:1274) carries overflow-wrap:anywhere but .revealwrap .who (1267) and .event (1268) do not, so an email-style name pasted from a distribution list scrolls the page sideways, measured 33px at 320px for 'ana.smith@marketingdepartment.com', and at 414px the threshold is 26 unbroken capitals (32px), rising to 255px at 40. Separately, init() only reads location.hash once (app.js:138), so pasting a reveal link into the address bar of an already-open tab changes nothing at all, no hashchange listener exists. Add overflow-wrap:anywhere to both lines and a hashchange handler.
fixes.where: index.html:1267-1268 (.who and .event), apps/secret-santa/app.js:138-141 (hash read once at init)

fixes.title: Name the pair that makes a draw impossible
fixes.rationale: Verified: with three people and one no-match pair the app correctly detects impossibility in 40ms, then says 'Those no-match rules make a draw impossible, remove one pair and try again', and the message contains neither 'Ana' nor 'Marcus'. The research lists this as table stakes with the gap called out explicitly: 'when the rules are mathematically unsolvable, name the specific pair causing it and offer the fix, rather than failing generically.' With the pair list already in memory, a single greedy pass that drops one pair at a time and retries identifies the culprit in milliseconds at these group sizes.
fixes.where: apps/secret-santa/app.js:90-96 (the generic impossibility message), helpers.js:20-40 (drawNames returns only null)

audit.purpose: A two-audience, no-backend Secret Santa draw. The ORGANIZER types an event name, an optional budget and a newline-separated roster, taps pairs of names to create no-match rules (couples, roommates), and presses Draw; the app shuffles until it finds a valid derangement and renders one row per person with a paste-ready message and a QR. The PARTICIPANT opens a per-person URL whose fragment carries a base64 payload of exactly their own name, their match, the event and the budget, and taps once to uncover it. No account, no email, no network call, no storage of any kind, the match travels inside the link. Roughly 95% of sessions are the second audience.
audit.structure: Two mutually exclusive views inside one document, toggled by .hidden. body > div.wrap containing: (1) header.app (index.html:1282-1287), 32px icon.svg with alt="", h1 'Secret Santa', span.spacer, a#tipLink.tipbtn.hidden un-hidden by JS; sws-prefs.js injects button#swsPrefsBtn into this row at runtime, so it is absent from source. (2) main#main (1289) wrapping both views. ORGANIZER (div#organizer, 1292-1325): three section.card blocks, card A (1293-1306) holds a .row of two label.f fields (#eventInput maxlength=60 with inline style="flex:1.5", #budgetInput maxlength=30), then h2 'Who's in?' and an UNLABELLED textarea#names with a four-line placeholder; card B (1308-1313) holds h2 'Who shouldn't draw each other? (couples, roommates)', a 51-character sentence rendered by the base as a 12px uppercase micro-label, a p.sub instruction, div.chips#exclPicker (EMPTY in source) and ul.plain#exclList (EMPTY in source); card C (1315-1324) holds button#drawBtn.btn.primary with inline width:100%/font-size:1.05rem, p.warn.hidden#drawWarn, and div#results.hidden containing an h2, ul.plain#linkList (EMPTY in source) and a p.hint carrying the honesty note. REVEAL (div#reveal.hidden, 1328-1336): div.revealwrap > div.who#revealWho, div.event#revealEvent, button#revealBtn, div.revealName.hidden#revealName, div.revealNote.hidden#revealNote. Outside .wrap: div#toast[role=status][aria-live=polite] (1340), footer.colophon with two inline-styled links (1341), and dialog#qrDlg (1343-1347) with an inline-styled h3, canvas#qrCanvas 300×300 and button#qrClose. Scripts: sws-prefs.js and sws-ui.js as blocking classic scripts in head; vendor-qrcode.js as a classic script exposing global qrcode(); app.js as a module. There is NO skip link, NO noscript, NO .trust stamp, NO .empty state, NO print affordance and NO persistence layer. Flow: init() (app.js:132) reveals the tip link, and if location.hash matches /^#r\./ AND decodes, calls showReveal() and RETURNS, the organizer listeners are never wired on a reveal page. Otherwise it wires the names input handler, the draw button, calls renderExclusions() and registers the service worker.

audit.dynamicMarkup:
Three containers are empty in source and entirely JS-built, so a restyle reading only index.html sees none of it. (A) #exclPicker, renderExclusions() (app.js:49-66) calls picker.replaceChildren() then appends one `` per name, or `class="chip sel"` for the pending pick. NO aria-pressed, NO aria-label, NO role beyond button, and the selected state exists ONLY as the .chip.sel class. The whole picker is destroyed and rebuilt on every single tap, which is why keyboard focus lands on after each selection. Renaming .chip or .sel silently breaks the state display with no error. (B) #exclList, same function (app.js:67-75) appends `
  • A ⛔ B
    • `. Every remove button carries the identical aria-label. Note the render skips pairs whose names are no longer present (app.js:70) while splicing by the true array index, so the index arithmetic stays correct, but the input handler at app.js:144 has already hard-deleted such pairs from `exclusions` anyway, which is how renaming a person silently destroys their no-match rule. (C) #linkList, draw() (app.js:101-113) appends per person `
  • Santa
    • `. Both buttons are named identically for all N people. The reveal URL exists ONLY inside the click closure, it is never written to the DOM, never a real , and therefore never printable, never long-pressable, never right-click-copyable, and invisible to a screen reader. (D) Runtime text writes: showReveal() (app.js:118-130) sets textContent on #revealWho, #revealEvent and #revealName and removes .hidden from #revealName / #revealNote while adding it to #revealBtn. All user text goes through textContent or el()'s `text` key, never innerHTML, which is why the injection payloads render as literal characters. (E) Canvas mutation: showQr() (app.js:158-173) fills #qrCanvas at a fixed 300×300 with #fff then #000 rects at floor(300/(count+8)) px per module. The white ground is painted by the canvas itself, so the code survives dark mode even though the dialog chrome does not. (F) el() helper (app.js:9-23): key 'class' → className, 'text' → textContent, keys starting 'on' → addEventListener, everything else → setAttribute. There is no hook for a class prefix; restyling means editing call sites. (G) Class toggles: .hidden on #organizer, #reveal, #results, #drawWarn, #revealBtn, #revealName, #revealNote, #tipLink; .show on #toast; .sel on chips. Renaming .hidden breaks the entire view switch.

comfortDefects.issue: The exclusion chips, the app's differentiating control, render 28px tall with 13px text and an 8px gap, and reach only 39px at Largest text + Roomy spacing. The 44px floor is never met at any setting, because .chip sizes from padding rather than min-height.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:654 (.chip, no min-height) instanced at app.js:53-56; measured 28px default / 39px at data-text=xxl + data-density=roomy
comfortDefects.fix: min-height:var(--tap) on #exclPicker .chip plus align-items:center. This is the one control the comfort panel currently cannot help.

comfortDefects.issue: .btn.small hardcodes min-height:36px, so all three row controls, 'Copy their message' 153×36, 'QR' 45×36, 'Remove pair' 37×36, stay at 36px even when the user has turned text up to 150%.
comfortDefects.fix: min-height:max(36px, calc(36px * var(--ui-scale))) at minimum, or promote the row controls to full .btn on touch pointers. The panel's contract is that turning text up never shrinks a target, here it simply fails to grow one.

comfortDefects.issue: The app-layer .warn override sets font-size:.85rem (measured 13.6px) and colour --accent, giving 3.66:1 against the base warn ground. Both the 16px body floor and the 4.5:1 contrast requirement fail, on the only error message in the app.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:1264, overriding the base .warn at index.html:679-687; instanced at index.html:1317
comfortDefects.fix: Delete the override. The base .warn box is already correct; the app only needs margin-top:var(--s3).

comfortDefects.issue: Six app-layer rules use raw px and rem outside the spacing and type scales, .revealwrap padding 36px 10px, #revealBtn margin 26px / padding 20px 30px / border-radius 16px, .revealName margin 20px 0 6px, plus five inline style attributes in the markup (flex:1.5, margin:0 0 8px, width:100%/font-size:1.05rem, margin-top:14px, margin-top:10px).
comfortDefects.fix: Map to --s* and --t-* tokens. DESIGN-SYSTEM.md rule 1: 'Tokens only, no hex, no rgb(), no magic px outside the spacing scale.'

comfortDefects.issue: index.html:1344 hardcodes color:#111 on the QR dialog heading, and #qrDlg sets no background token, so dark mode renders 1.01:1, the heading is invisible.
comfortDefects.fix: background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink); border:1px solid var(--line). Never a hex in the app layer.

comfortDefects.issue: The reveal name is 2.2rem (35.2px) where the category research specifies 2.5 to 3rem for one-glance legibility at arm's length. The reveal is the screen ~95% of users see and the only one most of them see.

The second card's h2 is a 51-character sentence, 'Who shouldn't draw each other? (couples, roommates)', rendered by the base as 12px uppercase with 0.9px tracking, which the design system explicitly reserves for labels and forbids for sentences.
comfortDefects.fix: Shorten the h2 to 'No-match rules' and move the sentence into the existing p.sub below it.

navigationDefects.issue: No skip link. .skip is shipped in the base (index.html:849) and #main exists (1289), but no anchor instance is present, so a keyboard user tabs through the comfort button and the tip pill on every visit.

The hash is read exactly once, at init. There is no hashchange listener, so pasting a reveal link into the address bar of a tab that already has the app open does nothing at all, verified: the reveal view stayed hidden until a full reload.

A malformed reveal hash falls through silently to the organizer view. Four variants tested, four silent falls-through with no error state, leaving a participant looking at 'Who's in?' and a Draw button.

The reveal view is a dead end in the other direction too: there is no route back to the organizer, no link to the studio hub from within it beyond the shared footer, and no indication that this page is part of a larger tool.

Editing the roster after a draw hides #results, and there is no way to bring it back except a redraw that changes every assignment. The only path from 'I made a typo' to 'I have my links again' destroys the exchange.

Reveal URLs live only inside click closures, they are never rendered as <a href>, so they cannot be long-pressed, right-click-copied, printed, or opened in a new tab. The single copy button is the only exit.
No empty state. Opened cold, the exclusion card is a 12px uppercase heading over an instruction and two empty containers, with nothing explaining that it activates only once names are typed.
navigationDefects.where: index.html:1308-1313; the base .empty component at index.html:711 is unused

a11yDefects.issue: textarea#names has no accessible name: 0 associated labels, aria-label null, aria-labelledby null, placeholder only. This is the standard battery's single hard failure and it is the app's most important field.
a11yDefects.wcag: 1.3.1 / 4.1.2 (and 3.3.2, the instruction disappears on first keystroke)

a11yDefects.issue: Exclusion chips carry no aria-pressed and no accessible state; selection is conveyed only by the .chip.sel accent fill. Measured aria-pressed null on a selected chip.

Every chip tap destroys the focused button, renderExclusions() calls picker.replaceChildren(), leaving document.activeElement === BODY. Measured directly. A keyboard user must re-tab the whole page between the first and second half of a pair.

#drawWarn has role null and aria-live null, and the impossible-draw path returns before the toast, so both failure modes are completely silent to assistive tech. Verified with a 3-person / 1-pair configuration.
All N 'Copy their message' buttons, all N 'QR' buttons and all N 'Remove pair' buttons share one accessible name each. The distinguishing text sits in a sibling span with no association.

canvas#qrCanvas has no aria-label, no role and no fallback text, and dialog#qrDlg has neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby despite containing an h3. The QR content is entirely unavailable non-visually, with no text alternative for the URL it encodes.

The draw succeeds without moving focus or announcing scope: focus stays on #drawBtn, N new rows appear below, and the toast says only 'Names drawn! Send each link privately.', no count, no heading focus.

Heading order is h1 → h2 in both cards → h3 inside the QR dialog, which is fine, but the h2s are styled as 12px uppercase micro-labels so the visual hierarchy does not match the semantic one, and the reveal view contains no heading at all, a screen-reader user landing on a reveal link has zero headings to navigate by.
Contrast: #drawWarn text 3.66:1 (13.6px, needs 4.5:1); QR dialog h3 1.01:1 in dark mode. Everything else measured passes, .revealName 6.88:1 light / 7.72:1 dark, .revealNote 5.66:1.

Positive: axe (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa) returns 0 violations on the organizer screen after a full draw with exclusions, and 0 on the reveal screen both covered and uncovered at Largest text. Every defect listed above is invisible to automated testing, they are state, naming and focus defects.

audit.printSupport: None of its own. The app adds zero @media print rules; only the base block at index.html:1190-1246 applies. Measured on a completed six-person draw: header, tip pill, toast, #swsPrefsBtn and #swsPrefs are correctly suppressed, but #results prints as six rows reading 'Ana Copy their message QR', the reveal URLs appear nowhere in the printed text (they exist only in click closures), textarea#names prints the full roster, and #drawBtn prints as a bordered box. The resulting sheet exposes who is in the exchange and conceals every assignment, the precise inversion of the app's purpose. The reveal screen prints acceptably (the name renders as pine text, legible without background graphics), but there is no print affordance anywhere in the UI and nothing resembling the fold-over Paper Mode the category research names as this app's strongest unclaimed differentiator.
riskyToRestyle: .hidden is the entire view-switching mechanism, #organizer, #reveal, #results, #drawWarn, #revealBtn, #revealName, #revealNote and #tipLink are all toggled by it. Renaming or weakening it (dropping the !important, replacing it with a [hidden] attribute) shows the participant the organizer tool and the organizer an empty reveal page, with no error.

.chip.sel (index.html:1262) is the ONLY signal that a name is pending pairing. Retiring it in favour of .chip.on or an [aria-pressed] selector, without also editing app.js:54, leaves the two-tap flow with no feedback whatsoever.

Every generated control is styled by class alone, .chip, .btn.small, .grow. app.js has no class-prefix hook (the el() helper at app.js:9-23 writes className directly), so any rename to .pill / .button--sm / .flex-grow leaves the chips, the row buttons and the name truncation unstyled at once.

The app-layer .warn at index.html:1264 only partially overrides the base .warn at 679, it replaces colour, size and margin while inheriting the box, border and left rule. Deleting the base rule and keeping the override yields bare 13.6px cranberry text with no container; deleting the override is the correct move and is a visible change.

#revealBtn is styled by ID with a 2px dashed border and its own padding, entirely outside .btn. A sweep that normalises buttons to .btn will either miss it (leaving one unstyled outlier on the app's most important screen) or flatten the deliberate 'unopened envelope' look that is the one moment of ceremony in the product.

The reveal rules reach through the legacy aliases --muted and --card (index.html:1267-1275). Those resolve via var() to --ink-2 and --surface, but a cleanup that drops the alias block at index.html:82-92 silently unsets three colours on the reveal screen.

#qrCanvas is painted imperatively at a fixed 300×300 with literal #fff/#000 fills (app.js:162-169). CSS cannot retheme it, and a rule that scales the canvas element without changing its attributes will resample the modules and can break scanning.

app.js:112 selects the QR button positionally in tests and app.js:107-113 builds each row as span + two buttons in fixed order. Any restructure into a two-line row or a wrapping .cluster must keep .grow first, because ul.plain .grow (index.html:702) is the only thing giving long names an overflow-wrap.
